subject: Airlock vs Shared Slate — sizing, procurement path & fallback for Nightingale pilot
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@nightingalehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nightingalehealth.com, security@nightingalehealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot hosting - isolation requirements and capacity

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We liked Redwood's perf numbers but our security team has pushed us to evaluate an "airlock" (fully private/VPC-on-prem style) deployment versus a dedicated reserved GPU pool in the cloud.

High level asks from Nightingale:
- P95 latency under 300ms for clinical inference mix (avg 350 tokens / request)
- Tenant isolation (HIPAA + EU data residency for subset)
- Predictable monthly cost for Q4 pilot (expected 250k inference calls/month)

Can you put together a short comparison (size, procurement path, timeline, escape-hatch for burst) so we can feed into procurement and security? Also include the ops assumptions (patching window, SLA credits, rollback plan).

Sara
Sara Bennett
Director, Data & AI
Nightingale Health

--
Note: procurement@nightingalehealth.com is on copy for scheduling the contracting discussion.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@nightingalehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Airlock vs Shared Slate — preliminary sizing & procurement path (see attachments)

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a spreadsheet with line-item sizing (A100/H100 options), cost math, and an operational checklist. Key takeaways up front:

1) Sizing summary (pilot profile — 250k calls/month, avg 350 tokens):
   - Dedicated reserved pool (cloud): 4 x H100S-80GB nodes sustained -> supports ~220 qps burstable through shared burst pool; expected P95 ~240ms w/ batching & prefix caching.
   - Airlock / Private (VPC+managed on customer subnet): 3 x A100-80GB (NVLink) on prem OR 2 x H100S for denser concurrency; slightly higher OPEX due to ops hours and networking egress controls.

2) Procurement & timeline:
   - Dedicated (reserved): 2-4 week onboarding after PO + network allowlist — Redwood handles runtime.
   - Airlock/private: 6-10 week delivery (customer infra prep + security review + onsite install if required).

3) Escape hatch / burst model:
   - Hybrid fallback: primary private pool + Redwood-hosted shared burst pool enabled. When private capacity hits 85% sustained, requests route to dedicated cloud nodes (encrypted, contract-scoped).

4) Ops & SLAs:
   - Private: customer-managed kernel/host patching windows; Redwood provides control-plane SLA and on-call integration.
   - Dedicated: Redwood-managed infra with monthly SLA (99.9) and standard SLA credit ladder.

I've put a recommended baseline for the pilot in the attached workbook (airlock_sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx). Marissa will follow up with contract language and a draft mutual action plan. Vivek will add the fallback routing policy for bursts.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Airlock vs Shared Slate — contract path & minimal redlines

Sara — following up on timing and commercial options. Two vendor paths we recommend for the pilot:

Option A — Dedicated Reserved (best time-to-value):
- Commercial: monthly consumption + 12-week rolling reserved credit (pilot commit).
- Contract asks: standard SOC 2 attestation, data processing addendum, limited liability cap aligned to pilot value.
- Procurement timeline: PO -> legal review -> onboarding (2–4 weeks).

Option B — Airlock/Private (strongest control):
- Commercial: one-time platform licensing + annual support, optional on-prem installation fees.
- Contract asks: on-prem access rules, HSM/KMS key ownership, runbook acceptance testing window.
- Procurement timeline: legal & security review more extensive (6–10 weeks).

We can stage: start pilot on Dedicated Reserved for Q4 while parallelizing the security review for Airlock. If security sign-off completes, migrate to private later in pilot (we'll include migration checklist). This minimizes time-to-insight while satisfying security's long-run posture.

I'll draft the minimal redlines for both paths and share a DocuSign-ready contract once you confirm preferred path.

—Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Ops, Redwood Inference

- Procurement: For Dedicated Reserved, what is the minimum commit and what's the penalty for early termination during a pilot? Also please itemize typical lead times for purchases in case our PO needs to specify a delivery window.

If you can answer those, procurement can draft a PO and security can triage the airlock checklist.

Sara

Subject: Re: Airlock vs Shared Slate — encryption & termination detail

Sara — quick answers to the two asks below (happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer):

1) Encryption / PHI boundary (hybrid fallback):
   - No plaintext PHI leaves the customer's VPC. Requests destined for Redwood-hosted burst nodes are sent using end-to-end TLS and use customer-managed envelope keys (KMS) for payload-level encryption. Payloads are decrypted only inside ephemeral, isolated inference containers with disk encryption and no persistent logs. Any retained telemetry is pseudonymized and limited to token counts and latency metrics (no message bodies). We will add a SLA clause guaranteeing no plaintext retention.

2) Dedicated Reserved commercial specifics:
   - Minimum pilot commit: one month at pilot baseline (recommended). Early termination: pro-rated refund for unused reserved credits after a 30-day notice; standard termination fee equals one month of committed spend if terminated inside first 60 days (we can soften for pilot with CF delivery SLA).
   - Lead times: once PO accepted, typical provisioning and onboarding is 7–21 days depending on allowlist complexity and region.

3) Additional ops notes:
   - Migration path: we provide a KV cache snapshot + prompt set migration tool to cutover without long cold-starts; expected cutover < 2 hours for stateful workloads.

I'll push a one-page security checklist to the Drive link and update the workbook with KMS flow notes.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
